data.title: Dalmia Bharat to buy back shares worth ₹700 crore; sets ₹1,850 price ceiling
data.description:
Dalmia Bharat has approved a share buyback worth up to ₹700 crore through the open market at a maximum price of ₹1,850 per equity share.

The company's board approved the buyback at a meeting held on November 23. The offer will cover fully paid-up equity shares with a face value of ₹2 each, excluding shares held by promoters, promoter group members and persons in control.

The company will buy back shares at a price of up to ₹1,850 apiece, with the total buyback amount capped at ₹700 crore, excluding related expenses.

The buyback will open on or before December 2, 2026. Once it opens, Dalmia Bharat will place buy orders through its broker on the stock exchanges' normal trading segment, purchasing shares at or below the maximum buyback price.

The company has said it will utilise at least 75% of the maximum buyback size, or ₹525 crore, towards the buyback. It will also deploy at least 40% of the maximum amount, or ₹280 crore, during the first half of the 66 working days from the buyback's opening date.

Promoters, promoter group members and persons in control will not participate in the buyback, the company said in its exchange filing.

Dalmia Bharat has constituted a buyback committee to oversee the process and appointed Company Secretary and Compliance Officer Rajeev Kumar as the compliance officer for the buyback.

According to the company's September 2026 shareholding pattern, promoters and the promoter group held 55.84% of Dalmia Bharat, while public shareholders owned 44.16%. Mutual funds held 15.59% and foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) owned 7.36%.

Dalmia Bharat shares ended 2.78% lower at ₹1,492 on the NSE on Friday, November 27, falling ₹42.70 during the session. The stock has declined 30.16% so far in 2026, shedding ₹644.20 from its previous year-end level.

data.title: Norse Atlantic's Norwegian Operating Unit Declares Bankruptcy
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Norse Atlantic said its Norwegian operating unit has filed for bankruptcy, while the parent company continues efforts to secure short-term financing.

The budget long-haul carrier has been exploring a potential sale, merger or partnership for several months and is currently in talks with investors over a possible takeover that would include a financing solution.

"Despite extensive efforts, the company has so far not been able to secure sufficient funding to meet its short-term liquidity needs," the company said in a statement.

The carrier, which operates two subsidiaries--Norse Atlantic Airways AS and Norse Atlantic U.K.--said Friday that the board of Norse Atlantic Airways AS has concluded there is no longer a basis for continued operations.

Earlier in the day, Norse Atlantic said the lessors of its entire fleet of 12 Boeing 787 Dreamliners had moved to terminate their leasing agreements.

"The board, management and advisers of the listed entity Norse Atlantic ASA and the UK subsidiary are working to find a solution for the remaining part of the business to continue operations," said Norse Atlantic Chief Executive Eivind Roald.

All Norse flights have been canceled and ticket sales have been discontinued. A message on its website warns passengers not to travel to airports for canceled flights, adding that customer service is no longer available by phone, email, chat or social media.

data.title: SemiLEDs Reports Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year End 2026 Financial Results
data.description:
SemiLEDs Corporation (), “SemiLEDs” or the “Company,” a developer and manufacturer of LED chips and LED components, today announced its financial results for the fourth quarter and full fiscal year 2026, ended August 31, 2026.

Revenue for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was $6.4 million, compared to $9.1 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026. GAAP net income attributable to SemiLEDs stockholders for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was $640 thousand, or $0.08 per diluted share, compared to a net income of $1.5 million, or $0.18 per diluted share, in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

GAAP gross margin for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 decreased to 23%, compared to 27% for the third quarter of fiscal 2026. Operating margin for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 decreased to 7%, compared to 16% for the third quarter of fiscal 2026. The Company’s cash and cash equivalents were $4.6 million at August 31, 2026, compared to $6.0 million at the end of the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

Revenues for fiscal year 2026 decreased to $19.1 million, compared to $43.0 million in fiscal year 2025. GAAP net income attributable to SemiLEDs stockholders for fiscal year 2026 was $817 thousand, or $0.10 per diluted share, compared to a net loss of $1.1 million, or $(0.15) per diluted share, in fiscal year 2025.

GAAP gross margin for fiscal year 2026 increased to 21%, compared to 6% for fiscal year 2025. Operating margin for fiscal year 2026 was 0.1%, compared to negative 4% in fiscal year 2025. The Company’s cash and cash equivalents were $4.6 million as of August 31, 2026, compared to $2.6 million as of August 31, 2025.

In fiscal years 2026 and 2025, the Company entered into a number of buy-sell orders for equipment that it purchased and then sold to its customers, and the Company anticipates continuing to receive buy-sell purchase orders in fiscal year 2027. As a result of these purchase orders and the associated uncertainty of the business, the Company’s revenue, cost of revenues, receivables, inventories and customer deposits may vary significantly over future quarters.

About SemiLEDs

SemiLEDs develops, manufactures, and sells light emitting diode (LED) chips, LED components, LED modules, sensor components incorporating LED or vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser (VCSEL), and systems. Its products are used for general lighting and specialty industrial applications, including ultraviolet, or UV, curing of polymers, LED light therapy in medical/cosmetic applications, counterfeit detection, germicidal and virucidal devices, LED lighting for horticulture applications, architectural lighting, entertainment lighting, and sensing of pressure or distance using LED or VCSEL.

data.title: Tether buys $10 million of Bitdeer shares as stock hovers near all-time low
data.description:
Tether bought about $10 million of Bitdeer Technologies Group (BTDR) shares on Nov. 25 as the bitcoin (BTC) miner traded near an all-time low, according to an amended Schedule 13D filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday.

Tether Investments bought 3.72 million Class A shares in two open-market transactions, according to the filing’s transaction schedule. The purchases included 12,240 shares at $2.65 and 3.7 million shares at $2.693, for a weighted average of about $2.69.

The purchases brought Tether’s holdings to 41.45 million shares, per the filing. This position gives the stablecoin giant shared voting and dispositive power over a reported 17.9% of Bitdeer’s outstanding Class A shares.

Bitdeer shares are trading at around $2.93 in early market trading on Friday, down 3.9% from Wednesday’s close, according to The Block’s BTDR price page. The stock is down 61.5% over the past month and 74.3% year to date after touching $2.60 on Wednesday, its 52-week low.

Tether’s share count has risen nearly 10% from the 37.73 million shares the USDT issuer disclosed in June. However, the company's reported ownership percentage declined from 19.7% because Bitdeer’s outstanding Class A shares increased to 231.8 million as of Sept. 30 from 191.2 million.

Earlier this month, the bitcoin miner reported record third-quarter revenue of $320.7 million, up 89% year over year, while its net loss widened to $125.5 million from $30.1 million.

StoneX cut its Bitdeer price target to $15 from $22 on Nov. 18 after new U.S. chip export licensing requirements raised questions over the timing of GPU deliveries to Malaysia.

data.title: Artificial intelligence usage is exploding, yet spending is stalling. Why a foundational rule of economics is breaking.
data.description:
By Jules Rimmer

The so-called 'Jevons Paradox' is breaking down in the second half of 2026

The deceleration in spending growth on AI tokens is a major cause for concern among the frontier model developers

So-called Jevons Paradox - the 19th century theory which when applied to artificial intelligence holds that as token prices fall, usage increases enough to increase overall spend - is in danger of being broken.

So far in 2026, for instance, the volume of tokens used - each unit of compute - has risen 44 times - but the total spend is only up 7.6 times, according to OpenRouter, an aggregator of AI platforms.

In the third quarter that elasticity fell from 5.5 to 1.6, and fourth quarter-to-date that figure has dropped again to 1.2.

In a blog post OpenRouter says demand for the compute capacity is strong but buyers are able to deploy the resources more efficiently, without increasing their budget.

There is a precedent for this. In December 2024 and November 2025 there were dips but both of these were followed by recoveries once new model launches were rolled out.

Cheaper inference, by which it costs less money and requires less power to run a trained artificial intelligence model, does still generate huge usage, but it isn't proving that spending boost as enterprises become more conscious of their total AI spend.

Some of this uncertainty has been reflected in the perfomance of frontier model lab Anthropic (ANT). After listing at $83 last week the shares rallied as high as $115 but fell below the issue price this week. In early trading on Friday, the stock rose nearly 6%, topping $87.

OpenAI is not yet publicly traded, but minority investor SoftBank (JP:9984) has dropped 32% this year. On the crypto platform Hyperliquid, a token for OpenAI has gone from indicating a market cap of $1.7 trillion to now indicating a valuation of $1.2 trillion.

-Jules Rimmer

data.title: Yields rise as tech stocks extend rebound
data.description:
By Colin Barr

US Treasury yields rose on Friday, reflecting the latest shift in investor sentiment on the AI buildout that in recent months has swamped other dynamics in global markets.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose 3.8 basis points to 4.88% and the 2-year yield (US2YT=RR), more sensitive to expectations for Federal Reserve policy, rose 2.7 bps to 4.66%. The 10-year yield is essentially flat for the month, reflecting tension between expectations that the Fed will raise rates multiple times in coming months to tamp down inflation and investor fear that the unwind of the artificial intelligence trade could tighten financial conditions enough to hit consumer spending and slow growth.

On Friday, US stocks opened higher, extending the gains they made late on Wednesday after the Nasdaq 100 briefly fell 20% from its high last month. The Nasdaq Composite was up 0.9% and the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX was up 0.7%. Pullbacks that push markets near so-called bear market territory have frequently triggered strong rebounds in recent years, reflecting a buy-the-dip mentality that has broadly paid off for investors ever since the recovery from the 2008 financial crisis.

"Financial conditions are once again in focus in light of the dramatic swings in the US equity market," said Ian Lyngen, managing director and head of US rates strategy at BMO Capital Markets in New York.

"Stability would be a welcome reprieve in light of the performance of risk assets in recent weeks, although we’re not convinced that the tech sector has fully repriced to the array of uncertainties facing the AI buildout."

The US yield curve is now at its flattest since early last year, notes Jonas Goltermann, chief markets economist at Capital Economics. While there is some debate about how much signal there actually is in this indicator, Goltermann warns that "high short-term yields relative to long-term ones reflect a judgment among market participants that tight monetary policy will weigh on economic growth – and corporate earnings – further ahead."

Whatever drama Friday's holiday-shortened session brings, investors are already turning to next week's nonfarm payrolls report on Friday, just days before the December Fed meeting. Few expect the jobs report to reduce the pressure on the central bank to act at the coming meeting and the ones that follow it, Lyngen said in his weekly rates report.

"Our base case remains 25 bp hikes at the next three meetings (Dec, Jan, Mar), followed by an extended period on hold during 2027 as the Fed awaits the impact of a tighter policy stance," Lyngen said.

He said BMO remains bullish on Treasury investments and expects that stance to become even more constructive "once there are signs of strain within the real economy – a facet of the current stage of the cycle that has been conspicuously absent."

data.title: A million satellites? What SpaceX's Starmind could mean for Earth and space
data.description:
By Gianluca Lo Nostro and Mirko Miorelli

The US Federal Communications Commission authorised Elon Musk's SpaceX on Wednesday to deploy 1 million satellites to support data centres in space, a fleet that would dwarf the total number of active satellites currently orbiting Earth.

The FCC said it was approving the SpaceX Starmind constellation to help meet rapidly growing demand for AI computing.

SpaceX's Starlink pioneered the era of large satellite networks, known as megaconstellations, with rivals including Amazon and Chinese operators developing similar systems.

But putting satellites into orbit on the scale envisaged by Starmind would take the boom to a new level, intensifying concerns among scientists about space junk, atmospheric pollution and the transformation of the night sky.

SpaceX did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment on this story early in the US day.

Here are some environmental questions surrounding projects such as Starmind:

WHAT WOULD 1 MILLION SATELLITES MEAN FOR THE ENVIRONMENT?

Scientists and regulators disagree over how much environmental damage Starmind could cause and how much can be known before the satellites, each with a wingspan of 75 metres (246 feet), begin flying.

In a recent study, University College London researchers estimated that 1 million satellites could increase emissions from launches and re-entries by roughly 70 to 150 times from current levels.

They said the resulting emissions could affect ozone, climate and air quality, and that SpaceX's filing lacked the information needed to fully assess those risks.

The FCC, however, said those questions largely fell outside its remit.

"Potential concerns related to the emissions of rocket launches and the subsequent impacts on the human environment as an indirect result of the Starmind system are outside of the Commission’s purview," the regulator said.

It also dismissed concerns about satellites burning up in the atmosphere as insufficiently established.

"Other concerns, including impacts on the atmosphere caused by satellites burning up on re-entry, remain speculative and not supported in the record," the FCC said.

WOULD SPACE JUNK INCREASE?

Almost certainly.

Low-Earth orbit, where Starlink and the proposed Starmind satellites would operate, is already becoming increasingly congested, and experts say the amount of debris there would probably keep rising even if all space activity stopped today.

As of February 1, there were more than 231 million debris objects in orbit measuring between 1 millimetre and 10 centimetres (4 inches), according to the European Space Agency, which has repeatedly called for measures to reduce collision risks.

SpaceX told regulators in a later submission in response to the FCC that it would initially deploy satellites at lower altitudes for testing before moving them higher. It said onboard propulsion would enable collision-avoidance manoeuvres, station-keeping — keeping satellites in their assigned positions — and eventual deorbiting.

The company also said it would continue refining satellite designs to reduce collision risks and use controlled re-entries aimed over oceans. SpaceX said its satellites would be designed to burn up completely during re-entry.

But the sheer number of satellites changes the calculation.

University of Birmingham professor Hugh Lewis said even a failure rate of 1% could leave thousands of derelict satellites in orbit each year, which could increase the risk of collisions.

WHAT WOULD HAPPEN TO THE NIGHT SKY?

Scientists say it could change dramatically.

Following the FCC's approval, the American Astronomical Society said the proposed constellation would undermine decades of public investment in astronomical facilities and impair scientists' ability to study the universe.

Lewis said some of the Starmind satellites would be in "sun-synchronous" orbits and would always be illuminated, adding that they could contaminate astronomical images.

Visual simulations shared online by Virginia Tech aerospace professor Shane Ross show bands of satellites stretching across large portions of the sky, potentially outnumbering visible stars.

The FCC rejected requests for additional conditions, saying protection of optical astronomy falls largely outside its rules and that SpaceX's commitment to coordinate with the US National Science Foundation was sufficient.

IS IT REALISTIC TO SEND 1 MILLION SATELLITES TO SPACE?

Not quickly. It would be impossible for SpaceX to launch 1 million satellites at the same time. The largest number of payloads carried by a single SpaceX rocket is 143.

Satellite operators sometimes request approval for higher numbers of satellites than they intend to deploy to buy design flexibility.

For example, SpaceX sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites before it began deployment of that system. The growing network currently has just over 11,000 satellites in space.

The FCC authorisation requires the company to place its first Starmind satellite into orbit by November 2033, have half in orbit by 2038 and complete deployment by 2040. No operator has ever sent 1 million objects into space.

The proposed network is central to Musk's vision of moving energy-intensive AI computing into orbit with solar-powered data centres. However, SpaceX itself told investors ahead of its stock market listing that the ambition to build space-based data centres relied on unproven technology and may not be commercially viable.

data.title: Alligator Bioscience provides an update on the company's financial position
data.description:
Lund, Sweden, 27 November 2026 – Alligator Bioscience (Nasdaq Stockholm: ATORX) provides an update on the company's financial position following the completed rights issue and the sale of mitazalimab to Biossil

On 22 September 2026, Alligator announced the final outcome of the rights issue of units. Alligator initially received approximately SEK 58.8 million before issue costs and repayment of bridge loans of SEK 19 million.

In October 2026, Alligator sold all rights to mitazalimab, including its derivatives, to Biossil, Inc. Alligator received an upfront payment of USD 0.75 million and is eligible for milestone payments of up to USD 108 million, as well as mid-single-digit royalties on future sales. From closing, Biossil is responsible for all further development, manufacturing, and patent costs, which means that Alligator do not carry any future costs associated to mitazalimab. With the divestment of mitazalimab, milestones and royalties from HLX22 and mitazalimab represent the majority of Alligator's future value stream.

Following these transactions, Alligator assesses that its existing cash is sufficient to fund operations through 31 December 2027. The assessment does not take into account repayment of the loan from Fenja Capital (approximately SEK 7 million, due in June 2027) or any proceeds from exercise of the TO 15 warrants in January 2027.

Topline data from Henlius' Phase 3 study of HLX22 in first-line HER2-positive gastric cancer is expected in the second half of 2027.

The TO 15 warrants can be exercised for subscription of new shares from 8 to 22 January 2027.

Alligator will update the market when there is new material information. Alligator only comments on the HLX22 programme when updates are shared through official channels, such as by Henlius or in publicly registered clinical trial information. The same policy applies to any new material information relating to mitazalimab.
